# Maersk Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/maersk-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/maersk-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects container tracking and schedule data from maersk.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Maersk Shipping Data in 2026](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-maersk)
- **Code:** [`maersk.py`](maersk.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Schedule](results/schedule.json) · [Tracking](results/tracking.json)

## What it scrapes

- Maersk.com container, BL, and booking tracking
- Point-to-point schedule routes with vessels, voyages, transit times, and port calls

## Functions

- `scrape_schedule_search(from_location, to_location, from_rkst_code, to_rkst_code, departure_date)` → `ScheduleSearch`: Search maersk.com Point-to-Point schedules
- `scrape_tracking(tracking_number)` → `TrackingResult`: Scrape a container/BL/booking number from maersk.com's tracking widget.

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import maersk


async def main():
    tracking = await maersk.scrape_tracking("269124324")
    schedule_search = await maersk.scrape_schedule_search(
        from_location="2IW9P6J7XAW72",
        to_location="1JUKNJGWHQBNJ",
        from_rkst_code="CNSGH",
        to_rkst_code="NLROT",
        departure_date="2026-08-15",
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`VesselInfo`**: `name`, `code`, `flag_country`
- **`PortCall`**: `facility_code`, `geo_id?`, `estimated_arrival?`, `estimated_departure?`, `voyage_number?`, `service_name?`, `service_code?`
- **`RoutingLeg`**: `carriage_type`, `transport_mode`, `vessel?`, `origin`, `destination`, `transit_time?`
- **`ScheduleRoute`**: `route_id`, `route_code`, `route_direction`, `estimated_transit_time`, `estimated_transit_days?`, `vessel_name?`, `origin_facility?`, `destination_facility?`, `departure_time?`, `arrival_time?`, `service_name?`, `voyage_number?`, `legs`
- **`ScheduleSearch`**: `url`, `from_rkst_code`, `to_rkst_code`, `departure_date`, `route_count`, `routes`
- **`TrackingEvent`**: `location?`, `facility?`, `description`, `date?`, `vessel?`, `voyage?`, `is_current`
- **`TrackingContainer`**: `container_number?`, `container_type?`, `last_updated?`, `status?`, `current_location?`, `status_date?`, `events`
- **`TrackingResult`**: `tracking_number`, `origin?`, `destination?`, `containers`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`maersk.py`](maersk.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `rendering_wait` = `5000`: wait after the page rendered, in milliseconds

## Notes

Maersk.com can be difficult to scrape because of scraper blocking, so this scraper uses Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker) feature and browser rendering to capture the tracking and routings API responses.

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/maersk-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_scrape_tracking`, `test_scrape_schedule_search`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
